title: Minkä väristä: asking the colour of a substance
summary: For the colour of a substance, use minkä väristä. Minkä väristä maito on? — Maito on valkoista.
targetSkills: Minkä väristä: asking the colour of a substance
prerequisiteSkills: Minkä värisiä: asking about several things
objectives: Ask a substance's colour with minkä väristä.
Describe its colour using the singular partitive adjective.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which.
For the colour of a substance, use minkä väristä. Väristä is the singular partitive form in this question phrase. The substance subject stays in its basic form.
keyPoints: Distinguish one substance from one countable thing and from a plural group.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Use a singular partitive colour adjective: Maito on valkoista (“The milk is white”). For the taught -nen colour words, replace -nen with -sta/-stä: valkoinen → valkoista. Other supplied patterns include musta → mustaa and ruskea → ruskeaa.
A natural short reply to “Minkä väristä maito on?” is “Valkoista.” (“White.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
When correcting a substance's colour, retain the singular partitive colour forms. Negation does not turn the substance into a countable object.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use a singular partitive colour adjective for the substance description.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: valkoista means white here. Valkoinen changes -nen to -sta: valkoista.
ruskeaa means brown here. Ruskea + -a gives singular partitive ruskeaa.
punaista means red here. Punainen changes -nen to -sta: punaista.
vihreää means green here. Vihreä + -ä gives singular partitive vihreää.
keltaista means yellow here. Keltainen changes -nen to -sta: keltaista.
mustaa means black here. Musta + -a gives singular partitive mustaa.
sinistä means blue here. Sininen changes -nen to -stä: sinistä.

examples.finnish: Maito ei ole punaista. Maito on valkoista.
examples.english: The milk is not red. The milk is white.
steps: Maito: milk; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Maito stays in its basic form as the subject of a description.
ei: not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Ei is the singular third-person present negative verb.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
punaista: red; description of what the subject is like. Punainen changes -nen to -sta: punaista.
on: is; verb (the action or state). Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.
valkoista: white; description of what the subject is like. Valkoinen changes -nen to -sta: valkoista.
